newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Candidates prepare for Madagascar president vote.
newsitem.headline: Candidates prepare for Madagascar president vote.

text.p: Former Madagascar presidents Didier Ratsiraka and Albert Zafy on Thursday entered the final phase of the campaign for Sunday's presidential runoff election with Ratsiraka widely tipped to take 60 per cent of vote.
In the first round in November, none of the 15 candidates gained the required 50 per cent of the vote, forcing a second-round ballot between the two leaders.
Ratsiraka, a 60-year-old retired admiral, was president from 1975 to 1993 when he was ousted and replaced by Zafy, a medical professor, after an unprecedented wave of political unrest.
The campaign has been calm and no problems are anticipated when polling stations open on Sunday.

The election became necessary when the National Assembly took the unprecedented step last July of impeaching Zafy for exceeding his constitutional powers. The constitutional court upheld the parliamentary vote for impeachment.
Ratsiraka returned from 19 months of voluntary exile in France in September to contest the election.

If he wins, he will be only the second African president to return to power through a free vote since the transformation of African politics and restoration of multi-party democracy in most of the continent in the last five years.

In the West African state of Benin, former president Mathieu Kerekou, who held office from 1972 to 1991, returned to power earlier this year after defeating President Nicephore Soglo in free elections.
